candidates.source_name: EKR - Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (hirdetmények)
candidates.why_relevant: Mandatory e-procurement platform for Hungarian state-owned and municipal buyers (Magyar Posta, MÁV-START, Volánbusz, BKK, hospitals, municipal parking companies). Tender notices and contract-award notices name the winning vendor, quantities and contract value for ticket vending machines, parcel lockers, payment terminals and kiosks. Since mid-2024 it offers structured search and automated 'hirdetményfigyelés' e-mail alerts on saved criteria.
candidates.access_status: public web, free; some functions require registration
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic keyword search (jegykiadó automata, önkiszolgáló, kioszk, fizetési terminál, POS, csomagautomata, parkolóautomata) + CPV-code filters; subscribe to the automated notice-watch; scrape/export result lists and award notices

negative_findings.description: No Hungarian public source was found in this pass that identifies the hardware or software supplier behind the self-checkout estates of Tesco HU, Lidl HU or SPAR HU. Retailer press and trade media report unit counts and customer attitudes, never the vendor.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple hu-language searches on 'önkiszolgáló kassza bevezetés szállító' returned chain-vs-chain unit counts (Tesco ~1028, SPAR ~900, Lidl ~1300 reported 2025) and legislative debate, but no supplier attribution.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The largest single block of non-bank self-service demand in Hungary is vendor-opaque; competitive share for SCO hardware in HU cannot be inferred from open sources alone and will need registry filings, integrator references or trade-fair material.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Hungarian vending / self-service machine industry association website was identified in this pass (searched alongside OKSZ). Only the general retail association OKSZ was confirmed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Association-oriented hu query returned OKSZ and trade press only; no 'Magyar Vending Szövetség'-type body surfaced in results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: An unattended-retail association would be a high-value pointer to operators, suppliers and market sizing for cash-handling and vending payment; its absence from results is a coverage hole rather than proof of non-existence.

negative_findings.description: Hospital-sector self-service and payment kiosks (betegirányító kioszk, kórházi fizetőautomata, parkolás kórházi területen) produced no usable Hungarian hits in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: The combined parking/hospital query returned only municipal parking material; the search explicitly returned nothing on hospital payment automats.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Healthcare is named in the cell definition; it is currently uncovered, and hospital procurement is exactly the kind of activity that would sit in EKR rather than the press.

negative_findings.description: Utilities (MVM, water and district-heating providers) as buyers of bill-payment kiosks / befizetőautomaták were not covered by a dedicated search in this pass, so no utility-specific source is recorded.
negative_findings.result_summary: No query was run on 'MVM ügyfélszolgálat befizetőautomata' or equivalent within this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Utility customer-service points are a classic cash-in/kiosk buyer segment; leaving it unsearched understates non-bank payment-acceptance demand.

negative_findings.description: None of the listed URLs were liveness-verified by this agent; several (EKR search pages, MNV szerződéskereső, NAV list-file endpoint) are dynamic or parameterised and may behave differently to an automated fetcher.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sources were recorded from search-result metadata and result snippets; no fetch verdicts are asserted.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream verification must treat any 403/timeout on nav.gov.hu, ekr.gov.hu or mnv.hu as bot-defence, not as a dead source.

brief: For Hungarian non-bank self-service and payment-accepting buyers the source landscape splits cleanly in two. State-linked buyers (Magyar Posta, BKK, MÁV-START/Volánbusz, municipal parking companies, hospitals) are well documented through mandatory channels - EKR, the Közbeszerzési Értesítő, üvegzseb contract disclosures and their own press rooms - which name winning suppliers, quantities and contract values, and these should be the backbone of collection. Private buyers (Tesco, SPAR, Lidl, Auchan, MOL, FOXPOST/Packeta) are visible only through retailer press releases, Hungarian trade media (Trade magazin, Store Insider, economx/vg/index) and vendor or integrator reference pages, which quantify installed base but almost never name the supplier - the main evidence gap in this cell. Two regulatory registers, NAV's e-pénztárgép distribution licences and the metrology authority's cash-register approvals, act as a de facto whitelist of who may legally sell checkout hardware in Hungary and are the most under-used structured source here. Key uncovered areas remain healthcare, utilities, TED at EU level, and cash-handling as distinct from card acceptance.
